analysis: The only change in this PR is at line 699 of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift. The test-only stub SwitchSlotLanguageModel.prepare moves from the signature (cache:windowSize:) to (cache:state:prefill:). The new signature tracks a presumed MLXLMCommon LanguageModel protocol change. The stub returns .tokens(input.text) and newCache returns [], so it does no real inference, holds no weights, and does nothing with keys, attestation or the cache. The file is test-only, so it is not shipped in the provider binary and adds no production attack surface. I traced the surrounding tests (model-switch drain, coordinator barrier, rollback, hash reuse) and found no change to their assertions, so the existing coverage of the model-switch and weight-hash behaviour (T-012, T-027, T-053 context) is intact. Unverified: whether the production code and other LanguageModel conformers adapt to the new protocol signature, and whether the upstream mlx-swift-lm dependency bump (state/prefill parameters) changes any security-relevant behaviour such as prefix-cache or KV handling (T-041, T-028). Those sit outside the supplied evidence and would need review in the files that carry the dependency bump. No findings in this unit.
